doc_summary: A multi-author agenda defining 'secret loyalties' (covertly installed model allegiance to a principal) and arguing the threat is neglected but tractable, with five technical research directions. Owain Evans is a middle author, so stances are attributed to the paper; the content is mostly about auditing defenses rather than realistic eval design.

items.claim: Distrusts behavioral evaluations as a reliable detector of hidden objectives because models can detect when they are being evaluated, so passing evals is weak evidence.
items.quote: This also faces the general problem of eval-awareness where models can detect when they are being evaluated.

items.claim: Prefers matched-control, principal-specific behavioral evaluations over generic evals because loyalty only shows up in scenarios where the principal's interests are at stake and must be compared against baselines.
items.quote: A comprehensive evaluation protocol would need to test a prioritized set of principals across scenarios where their interests are at stake, using matched controls.

items.claim: Judges auditing evidence by whether it holds at realistic affordance levels; failures of black-box auditing and interrogation under such constraints count as meaningful evidence of the threat.
items.quote: Black-box auditing failed to distinguish these from baselines at realistic affordance levels, and direct interrogation never succeeded, even when auditors were told the loyalty's broad structure.

items.claim: Prefers building reproducible model organisms spanning a 2D space (activation breadth × action-space breadth) over studying only narrow backdoors because broader loyalties are the open and more dangerous case.
items.quote: Construct reproducible models with artificially instilled loyalties spanning the 2D space. Early work shows narrow variants are feasible; the open question is whether broader variants

items.claim: Distrusts content-level inspection of data and single-stage checks, since attacks can be split across stages and look innocuous in isolation.
items.quote: Content-level inspection alone is insufficient, and multi-stage attacks that split poisoning across pretraining and post-training may appear innocuous at each stage in isolation

items.claim: Prefers benchmarking existing defenses on the new threat model over inventing new methods first because a decade of backdoor-detection tools may or may not transfer.
items.quote: Test whether the backdoor detection, black-box auditing, white-box auditing, and mitigation techniques the ML community has developed over the past decade work on secret loyalties.

items.claim: Distrusts monitors and evaluation tools that share provenance with the system under test, since they can be compromised; wants independently sourced tooling.
items.quote: Safety monitors can themselves be compromised. If they do, defenders may need independently sourced monitoring infrastructure.

items.claim: Interpretability is framed as a well-defined target (special action-guiding status of an entity vs. controls), though hard to separate from ordinary entity knowledge.
items.quote: The target is well-defined: whether the model treats a specific entity as having special action-guiding status relative to controls.

items.claim: Open problem: whether loyalty can be detected and removed post hoc without knowing the trigger.
items.quote: Can loyalty be detected through interpretability (does the model treat an entity as having special action-guiding status?) and can it be removed without knowing the trigger?
